# Splinely

> Splinely is a vector animation tool: a desktop editor plus a command-line tool
> (`splinely-cli`) that creates `.sply` projects (compact binary by default, strict canonical JSON via `convert`/`cat`) with shapes, paths,
> keyframe animation, bones, state machines and embedded audio, and exports them
> as one self-contained interactive SVG. This file tells an LLM agent with shell
> access how to install the prebuilt binaries and start using them.

## Install (Linux x86_64, no compiling)

Prebuilt packages are attached to every GitHub release and run on Linux with
glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora 36+).

1. Find the latest release tag:
   `curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/wasser-quest/splinely/releases/latest`
   and read `tag_name` (for example `v0.3.0`).
2. Download the asset and its checksum, verify, then unpack:

   ```sh
   VERSION=v0.3.0   # use the tag_name from step 1
   NAME="splinely-${VERSION}-x86_64-linux"
   BASE="https://github.com/wasser-quest/splinely/releases/download/${VERSION}"
   curl -fLO "$BASE/$NAME.tar.gz" && curl -fLO "$BASE/$NAME.tar.gz.sha256"
   sha256sum -c "$NAME.tar.gz.sha256"
   mkdir -p ~/.local/opt && tar -xzf "$NAME.tar.gz" -C ~/.local/opt
   export PATH="$HOME/.local/opt/$NAME/bin:$PATH"
   splinely-cli --version
   ```

   Stop and report if the checksum does not match. Ask the user before adding
   the PATH line to their shell profile.
3. On macOS (`splinely-<tag>-aarch64-macos.tar.gz` / `-x86_64-macos.tar.gz`) or
   Windows (`splinely-<tag>-x86_64-windows.zip`) packages are configured but have
   NOT been tested on real hardware: tell the user, then follow
   docs/INSTALL-BINARIES.md if they agree. On any other OS or architecture there
   is no prebuilt package: offer to build from source (`cargo build --release`,
   see README.md).

## Package contents

- `bin/splinely-cli`: the command-line tool; use this for all authoring work.
- `bin/splinely`: desktop editor (GUI).
- `bin/splinely-viewer`: native player window; needs GTK 3 and WebKitGTK 4.1
  (`libgtk-3-0 libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0` on Ubuntu). Do not install system packages
  without asking the user.
- `bin/splinely-runtime`, `lib/libsplinely_runtime.so`, `include/splinely_runtime.h`:
  native runtime for embedding animations in other programs.
- `LLM.md`, `CLI.md`, `prompts/splinely-author.md`: authoring guides.
- SVG import (`import-svg`: text, gradients, data-URI images, structured report, limits, source/visual conflict state): https://github.com/wasser-quest/splinely/blob/main/docs/svg-import.md
- Accessibility of the web player/SVG (`splinely-cli a11y`, `check` warning `interactive_without_label`; supported/unsupported/unverified): https://github.com/wasser-quest/splinely/blob/main/docs/accessibility.md
- `examples/`: sample projects and exported SVGs.

## Using it

- Read `splinely-cli guide` and `LLM.md` before the first edit.
- Typical flow: `splinely-cli new --output scene.sply`, add shapes with
  `splinely-cli node add`, animate with `splinely-cli keyframe`, validate with
  `splinely-cli check scene.sply`, look at `splinely-cli render scene.sply --time 1 --output preview.png`,
  then `splinely-cli export scene.sply --output scene.svg`.
- Cannot view images? `splinely-cli inspect scene.sply --ascii` describes the
  picture as text: shapes back to front with colour words and positions,
  layout sentences (inside, overlaps, hidden behind, mirrored pairs), an ASCII
  grid with a legend, and an animation summary (`--node ID`, `--detail full`, `--crop`).
- `splinely-cli COMMAND --help` documents every command; output is JSON.
- Only pass `--trusted-js` to `export` when the user explicitly approves the
  project's custom JavaScript. The same applies to `export --plugin DIR`, which
  embeds a plugin's runtime JavaScript (hash-pinned, not a sandbox); `plugin apply`
  and `plugin validate` only touch declarative project data and are safe.
- If a command fails with error code `internal_error`, Splinely itself crashed.
  Tell the user and show them the `reportUrl` (a pre-filled GitHub issue they
  may submit). Never submit it yourself.
- Exported SVGs need a script-capable browser (open directly or via `<object>`,
  not `<img>`); audio starts only after a user click.
